title: Introduce inter-run-variance-heatmap + auto-repair-suggester CI hook
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We intermittently see prompts that are stable per-seed but vary significantly across evaluation runs (inter-run variance). These cases bypass current per-run gates and later cause customer-facing regressions. This PR adds a new inter-run variance heatmap reporter and a paired CI hook that can (optionally) auto-suggest repairs (paraphrases) for prompts that exhibit unstable semantics across runs.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a variance aggregation stage that collects per-prompt metrics across multiple evaluation runs (default: 5 runs, configurable). 2) Produces a compact heatmap visualization (text and JSON) keyed by prompt_id x metric, highlighting regressions and divergence patterns. 3) Adds a CI hook (ci-eval-variance) which fails the gated check when more than N prompts cross a configurable variance threshold for a given metric (default: 5 prompts / metric). 4) Implements an optional auto-suggest flow that generates candidate paraphrases via a small paraphrase model (redwood/paraphrase-small-v1) and scores them for reduced inter-run variance — suggestions are surfaced in the CI failure payload and in the Console alert for triage.

Design notes: - The variance calculation uses a bootstrap-of-seeds approach to estimate inter-run standard deviation while attenuating single-run outliers. - Heatmap buckets metrics (e.g., exact-match, semantic-similarity, BLEU-like scoring) into categorical severity bands (info/warn/critical). - Auto-suggest is intentionally conservative: it only proposes paraphrases when the top candidate reduces the measured variance by >= 30% and preserves the original expected label fidelity. Generated suggestions are marked as draft and must be reviewed before being applied to upstream prompt sets.

Backward-compatibility and safety: - The CI hook defaults to soft-fail on nightly branches and hard-fail on release/* branches. Teams can opt out per-prompt via a new prompt metadata flag (metadata: {"variance_allowlist": true}). - The engine that calls the paraphrase model uses rate-limited async calls and does not block the main evaluation pipeline; suggestions are computed post-run and attached to the CI artifact.

Operational impact: - Adds ~12% overhead to full cross-run smoke suites when running with default 5-run aggregation. We profiled this on our perf-canary cluster and observed stable memory behavior. - Telemetry: new metrics eval.variance.runs, eval.variance.per_prompt, and eval.variance.suggest_count (exposed in Console).

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests added for variance calculator and thresholding logic. - Integration test in tests/integration/ensure_variance_reporter.sh that runs a 3-run mock harness. - Nightly canary enabled first week (soft-fail). After 2 weeks of tuning, hard-fail turned on for release branches.

Docs: Added docs/eval/variance-heatmap.md with usage examples and configuration knobs.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of variance aggregator and heatmap reporter - [x] CI hook and infra wiring (ci/ci-eval-hooks.yml) - [x] Auto-suggest generator with safety checks - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Docs and canary rollout plan

Related: builds on ideas from ENG-1984 (prompt stability study) and complements the anchor-based replay hooks we've used previously.

release_notes: Adds an inter-run variance heatmap reporter to the eval harness with an optional auto-suggest reparative flow. New CI hook can block merges on unstable prompt sets; configurable thresholds and opt-outs available.
notes_for_ops: Enable the feature via eval.hooks.variance.enabled (default false in small teams). Watch eval.variance.per_prompt and set rate limits for paraphrase suggestions to avoid model cost spikes.
